facts.label: official
facts.quote: The Scheme, framed by the Reserve Bank in exercise of the powers conferred on it under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (10 of 1949), Section 45L of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (2 of 1934), and Section 18 of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 (51 of 2007), will provide cost-free redress of customer complaints involving deficiency in services rendered by entities regulated by RBI, if not resolved to the satisfaction of the customers or not replied within a period of 30 days by the regulated entity.
facts.text: Bank customers can escalate complaints free of cost to the RBI Integrated Ombudsman if the regulated entity fails to resolve the issue within 30 days.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: The complaint must be made to the RBI Ombudsman within 90 days from the date on which the above timeline expires or the date of the last communication from the concerned Regulated Entity, whichever is later.
facts.text: An aggrieved customer must escalate an unresolved banking complaint to the RBI Ombudsman within 90 days after the standard resolution window expires.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: Non-adherence to RBI/ System Provider instructions on payment transactions through Unified Payment Interface (UPI)/ Bharat Bill Payment System (BBPS)/ Bharat Quick Response (QR) Code, with 43.89% of complaints, was the major ground of complaints, followed by Mobile/ Electronic transfers (24.10%), non-reversal of funds due to wrong beneficiary transfer by the System Participant (8.79%) and non-adherence to RBI guidelines for PPIs (7.98%).
facts.text: Non-reversal of funds due to wrong beneficiary transfers represented 8.79 percent of maintainable grievances handled by digital transactions ombudsman offices in a reporting year.

facts.label: official
facts.text: For basic savings bank deposit accounts widely used for household budgeting, maximum customer liability in unauthorized electronic transactions reported between four and seven working days is capped at 5,000 rupees.

facts.label: official
facts.quote: • All other SB accounts • Pre-paid Payment Instruments and Gift Cards • Current/ Cash Credit/ Overdraft Accounts of MSMEs • Current Accounts/ Cash Credit/ Overdraft Accounts of Individuals with annual average balance (during 365 days preceding the incidence of fraud)/ limit up to Rs.25 lakh • Credit cards with limit up to Rs.5 lakh, 10,000.
facts.text: For standard savings bank accounts holding household salaries and savings, customer liability for third-party electronic fraud reported within four to seven days is limited to 10,000 rupees.

facts.label: reported
facts.quote: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has set a maximum ceiling of ₹1.5 per transaction for accessing the NUUP, although rates can differ among service providers.
facts.text: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India capped the cost of accessing UPI banking services offline over the USSD platform at 1.5 rupees per session.

intro.prompt: 9:16 vertical, 1080x1920, about 8 seconds, photorealistic and cinematic, bright vivid colour. Setting: close-up of a busy Indian bank branch counter in morning natural light, a young man's hand pressed flat on the counter in panic, an empty teller chair behind the glass. The background is real and in motion behind him (as fits the place: waves, mist, leaves, flags, lamps flickering, people walking, traffic, light shifting); never a still, flat or heavily blurred backdrop. Framing: medium shot from the waist up, his whole head and both shoulders inside the frame with clear space above his hair and on both sides, and he stays framed like this to the end; do not crop the top of his head. Lighting: warm key light on the face, a soft rim light on the hair, matched to the scene; flattering, no harsh shadows, no dull or flat grey look. SG [locked] standing relaxed and upright, shoulders open, wearing a black blazer over a white shirt, top button open. Speaks from the first frame, mouth matched to the words, steady eye contact with the lens. Face and delivery: a confident, charismatic documentary presenter. Calm, natural face with a pleasant, warm smile, relaxed eyebrows, eyes soft and focused on the viewer. On "wapas kyun nahi karta" the eyes narrow a little with intrigue and the head tilts slightly, as if sharing a secret. On "Suniye, twist yahan hai!" a warm, confident smile and one small nod. Natural blinking, subtle head movement. No exaggerated expressions: no wide eyes, no raised eyebrows, no open-mouth surprise, no big grin, no frown; never sad, gloomy, worried or tired. Voice: warm, clear, measured, with quiet intensity; a short pause before "wapas kyun nahi karta". Hands: one slow, small gesture toward the scene behind him on the first line, then hands rest; no fast or large arm movements. Camera: eye level, a very slight slow push-in, slight handheld feel. Empty hands, no prop. @SGLearning watermark in the top right corner, white, bold, 80% opacity. No captions, no subtitles, no other on-screen text. No hologram, no floating screen, no graph, no chart, no laptop, tablet, monitor, TV or glowing blue panel anywhere in the frame. Export at 1080x1920.
